title: Form Mt. Angel-Monitor Fire District and Set Tax Rate
ballot_label: Form Mt. Angel-Monitor Fire District and Set Tax Rate. Question: Shall District be formed with a permanent tax rate of $1.97 per $1,000 assessed value beginning fiscal year 2027-28?
summary: Would form the Mt. Angel-Monitor Fire District, combining the Mt. Angel Fire District and Monitor Rural Fire Protection District, effective January 1, 2027, only if both dissolution measures (24-526 and Clackamas 3-640) pass. Sets a permanent rate of $1.97 per $1,000 assessed value from July 1, 2027, replacing the two districts' rates. Employees and property transfer to the new district, governed by a five-member board elected November 3, 2026.
yes_means: A yes vote forms the Mt. Angel-Monitor Fire District with a permanent tax rate of $1.97 per $1,000 assessed value, effective only if both dissolution measures also pass.
no_means: A no vote does not form the new district; the Mt. Angel and Monitor districts continue to operate separately under their current tax rates.
fiscal_impact: New permanent property tax rate of $1.97 per $1,000 of assessed value, first levied for fiscal 2027-28 (collection beginning November 2027); per the explanatory statement it is higher than the existing permanent rate of each district, whose rates would no longer be levied. Neither district has bonded debt; consolidation creates no new debt.

collection_notes: yes_means/no_means: Oregon local ballot titles carry no official result-of-vote text, so these are neutral one-sentence descriptions written by the collector, grounded strictly in the official ballot question/summary. Contingency (official text): 24-526 (dissolve Mt. Angel Fire District, Marion), 3-640 (dissolve Monitor RFPD, Clackamas) and 24-529 (form Mt. Angel-Monitor Fire District) each take effect only if all three are approved. Arguments of kind 'explainer' on the YES side quote the rationale that the official ballot title/explanatory statement attributes to the sponsoring governing body; they are not filed pamphlet arguments. No comparable NO-side statement exists in the official text. Pamphlet access limit: WebFetch converts the Marion County voters' pamphlet PDF to only its first 118,524 characters (through p. 38, ending mid-sentence in the 24-528 explanatory statement); the Clackamas pamphlet (docs.clackamas.us/.../03f4f9db-...) is likewise cut off at p. C-33 in candidate statements. Pages 39-45 (remaining measures and any filed arguments) could not be read, so the existence of filed pamphlet arguments for 24-526, 24-528 (partly), 24-529, 24-530 and 24-531 is UNCONFIRMED; a verifier with full PDF access should check. Search budget: the shared WebSearch budget for this run was exhausted partway through step 3; the measure-number search was run for both sides, but the T3 allowed-domain search could not be run for either side. Equal effort was kept: the same searches ran for YES and NO. The district spans Marion and Clackamas counties; both counties list it as 24-529. Inventory source_url (Clackamas doc 5e9ffeb3) is the explanatory statement and was readable. Marion's own explanatory statement PDF for 24-529 is image-only. Inventory title matches the caption.
